title: Why branches?
concept: Try an idea without breaking main; git branch

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: We need to add a map to the site, but we cannot break the main page.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: A **branch** is a safe place to try an idea.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Here is the part everyone gets wrong at first.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: A branch is **not** a folder. It does not copy your files anywhere.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: A branch is just a label pointing at one commit. That is all it is.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Make one with `git branch map`, then run `git branch` to list them.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Watch the graph: a second label appears on the same commit. Nothing moved.

items.text: Create a new branch called map
Answer: what did making the branch do?
Answer: can you cd into a branch?

hints: Make the branch, then list your branches to see it.
`git branch <name>` creates a label. `git branch` on its own lists them.
Run `git branch map`, then `git branch`, then answer both questions.
recap: A branch is a label pointing at a commit, not a folder and not a copy of your files. `git branch <name>` makes one; `git branch` lists them.

questions.prompt: You ran git branch map. What happened to your files?

choices.text: Git copied them into a new folder called map
Nothing: a new label now points at the same commit
They were moved onto the map branch

questions.explanation: A branch is a label on a commit. Creating one writes a few bytes and touches none of your files.

questions.prompt: The output of git branch looks like a folder listing. Can you run `cd map` to enter the branch?

choices.text: Yes, cd map opens the branch
No: branches are not folders. You move between them with git switch

questions.explanation: `cd` moves between folders. Branches are labels inside git, so you move between them with `git switch`.
